answer: Because the age is read from the tundra checkpoint rather than self-declared, the vault audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. Running a farm as a result means funding each extra identity through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent forfeits once and never again. An identity must be at least 3 epochs old on the pigment ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. That is 6 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
